subject: botany
question_text: “Fertilization is not an obligatory event for fruit production in certain plants.” Explain the statement.

verification.note: Chapter 6 is sourced from the Junior Fastrack botany guide (book p.15), which prints the question and a model answer but NO star ranks and NO year citations. Only ONE source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely pending. The 2+1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK POSITION: the book's model answer inserts 'embryo develop from unfertilized diploid female gamete … known as parthenogenesis' as a separate bullet between parthenocarpy and apomixis; in the NCERT wording that diploid-egg path IS apomixis, so this card folds it into the apomixis step and gives banana as the standard parthenocarpy example the book omits.

insider_note: The statement is quoted from NCERT, and the expected core is parthenocarpy with banana; apomixis is the marker's plus point.

steps.label: Parthenocarpy
lines: In some plants the ovary grows into a
Ex: banana — the fruit is seedless.
steps.why: This is the direct answer to the statement: a fruit is a mature ovary, and in parthenocarpic plants the ovary matures without any fertilization.
common_mistakes: Writing parthenogenesis where parthenocarpy is meant — carpy = fruit (carpel); genesis = a new individual.
Leaving out the example — banana is the standard one.
steps.memory_tip: Carpel → parthenoCARPY = fruit without fertilization. Compare: parthenoGENESIS = offspring from an unfertilized gamete.
steps.margin_note: Definition + the word parthenocarpy + banana: that is the 2-mark core.

lines: fertilization: a diploid egg cell forms
without meiosis and develops into the
steps.why: Apomixis extends the statement from fruit to seed: even the seed can form without fertilization. The book labels this development of the unfertilized diploid egg 'parthenogenesis'; the plant phenomenon as a whole is apomixis (NCERT).
common_mistakes: Saying the apomictic egg is haploid — it is diploid because meiosis is skipped.
Mixing up apomixis (seed without fertilization) with parthenocarpy (fruit without fertilization).
steps.memory_tip: Mixis = mixing of gametes. Apo-mixis = away from mixing — a seed formed with no fusion of gametes.
steps.margin_note: Two lines on the diploid egg + one example.

steps.label: Conclusion

lines.text: Fruits and seeds can form without fertilization

lines: fertilization is not an obligatory event
steps.why: The question says 'explain the statement', so the answer must end by returning to the statement: two named phenomena prove it.
common_mistakes: Stopping after the two definitions without linking back to the statement.
steps.memory_tip: Parthenocarpy = FRUIT without fertilization; apomixis = SEED without fertilization.
steps.margin_note: One closing sentence naming both phenomena.
